items.subject: Computer Science
items.body: SDE Role: How do you find two numbers in a sorted array that add up to a target sum in O(N) time and O(1) extra space?

metadata.modelAnswer: Use the Two-Pointer approach. Initialize left pointer at index 0 and right pointer at N-1. Calculate currentSum = arr[left] + arr[right]. If currentSum == target, return [left, right]. If currentSum < target, increment left pointer. If currentSum > target, decrement right pointer. This runs in O(N) time and O(1) space.

items.subject: System Design
items.body: SDE Role: Explain the difference between Cache-Aside (Lazy Loading) and Write-Through caching strategies.

metadata.modelAnswer: In Cache-Aside, the application first reads from cache; on a cache miss, it reads from database, populates the cache, and returns data. In Write-Through, data is written to the cache and database simultaneously, ensuring cache consistency at the cost of higher write latency.

items.subject: Data Science
items.body: Data Role: What is the Bias-Variance Tradeoff and how do regularization techniques (L1 vs L2) mitigate it?

metadata.modelAnswer: Bias is error from erroneous assumptions (underfitting); Variance is error from sensitivity to small fluctuations in training data (overfitting). L1 (Lasso) regularization adds |w| penalty driving irrelevant weights to 0 (feature selection). L2 (Ridge) adds w² penalty shrinking weights smoothly.

items.subject: Business Analytics
items.body: Analyst Role: How would you calculate Month 1 User Retention Rate in SQL for an e-commerce platform?

metadata.modelAnswer: Join user signup date cohort table with active monthly orders table. Filter for users whose active order date month equals signup month + 1. Calculate Retention % = (Count of Active M1 Users / Total Signup Cohort Users) * 100.

items.subject: Behavioral Competency
items.body: Behavioral: Describe a situation where you had a technical disagreement with a team member on a project. How did you resolve it?

metadata.modelAnswer: Demonstrate constructive collaboration, active listening, and empirical benchmarking.

starFramework.situation: During our final year capstone project, my teammate wanted to use MongoDB while I advocated PostgreSQL for structured relational financial transactions.
starFramework.task: I needed to align our architecture choice without delaying the sprint timeline or harming team dynamics.
starFramework.action: I scheduled a 30-minute benchmarking session where we ran load tests on sample schema for both databases and evaluated ACID compliance requirements.
starFramework.result: The empirical benchmark showed PostgreSQL handled 40% faster transactional queries. We agreed on Postgres, completed the project 2 days ahead of schedule, and achieved an A grade.
